full_judgment: 2. This relates to removal of some unauthorized constructions from the periphery of Lalbagh Fort which was declared as historical monument. The High Court Division directed for protecting the Lalbagh Fort by removing unauthorized constructions from the periphery of Lalbagh Fort. Respondent claims that the disputed property is not located within periphery of Lalbagh Fort and that by successive deeds of transfer they are in possession as owners. The disputed house was recorded in the name of the predecessor of the respondents in the C.S. Khatian and pursuant thereto they have been paying rent and taxes to the authorities. The petitioner produced the C.S. map of the Lalbagh Fort, which clearly shows the disputed plot is located within the Lalbagh Fort complex. Since there is conflicting claim regarding the location of the disputed plot, this court directed the Archeology Department to report after a thorough survey by an expert committee constituting with a representative of Land Records and Survey Directorate, and a professor of Archeology Department of Jahangirnagar University. Pursuant to such direction, a report had been submitted on 22.05.2017 pointing out that during Mughal period, there was no existence of any house within the Lalbagh Fort, but sometimes thereafter the record was prepared, Hashem and others encroached into a portion of the Lalbagh Fort and claimed ownership. It is also stated that on physical inspection, it can be easily perceived that the disputed house is located within Lalbagh Fort and that the existence of the house has tarnished the beauty of the historical monument. It was clearly pointed out that Abul Hsahem encroached 0.027 and Md. Harun has encroached .0350 acre of land.
